nodes.name: paths.ts
nodes.summary: Config file discovery helpers: walks up from a directory to find opencode.json/jsonc config files, and computes the ordered, deduplicated list of config directories (global config path, per-level .opencode dirs, home directory, OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR override) used during config resolution.

nodes.name: files
nodes.summary: Effect generator that walks upward from a directory collecting `<name>.jsonc`/`<name>.json` config files until the worktree root, returned nearest-last so callers can merge in priority order.

nodes.name: directories
nodes.summary: Computes the deduplicated config directory list: the global config path, `.opencode` dirs found between the project directory and worktree root (unless project config is disabled), the home `.opencode` dir, and the OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR flag override.

nodes.name: permission.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the permission config schema: Action/Object/Rule schemas plus the Info transform that normalizes the shorthand action form (e.g. `"ask"`) into per-target rule objects (`{ "*": "ask" }`), exposing a derived zod schema for runtime config parsing.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Effect Schema decodeTo with SchemaGetter transforms; known permission keys (read, edit, bash, task, ...) get explicit struct fields while Schema.StructWithRest keeps arbitrary tool keys valid.

nodes.name: plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Plugin config helpers: discovers plugin files under `plugin(s)/` directories, resolves path-like plugin specs relative to the config file that declared them, and deduplicates merged plugin origins by load identity (npm package name or exact file URL) while preserving provenance.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Scans a directory for `{plugin,plugins}/*.{ts,js}` files (including dotfiles and symlinks) and returns them as file:// URL specs ready for dynamic import.

nodes.name: resolvePluginSpec
nodes.summary: Rewrites path-like plugin specs into absolute file:// URLs resolved against the declaring config file's directory (handling file://, absolute, and Windows drive paths), so later config merges cannot reinterpret relative paths against a different base.

nodes.name: deduplicatePluginOrigins
nodes.summary: Deduplicates merged plugin origins by load identity — package name for npm specs, exact file URL for local specs — with last-declared winning, while keeping the full Origin so downstream code knows which config file won.

nodes.name: provider.ts
nodes.summary: Effect Schema definitions for the `provider` config key: `Model` covers per-model capabilities, cost, context limits, modalities, and variant overrides, while `Info` covers provider-level options (apiKey, baseURL, enterpriseUrl, total vs SSE-chunk timeouts) and the provider's model map. Both carry derived zod schemas.

nodes.name: reference.ts
nodes.summary: Schema for the `reference` config key: a record of named entries that are either plain strings, git repository refs (with optional branch), or local directory paths, consumed when cloning reference material for context.

nodes.name: search.ts
nodes.summary: Schema for the `search` config key: `EmbeddingInfo` selects the embedding provider (local xenova/transformers on CPU or the OpenAI API) with model id, dimension, and API key; `SearchInfo` nests it for semantic search configuration.

nodes.name: server.ts
nodes.summary: Schema for the `server` config key controlling the HTTP server: port, hostname, mDNS service discovery toggles, custom mDNS domain, and additional allowed CORS origins.

nodes.name: skills.ts
nodes.summary: Schema for the `skills` config key: additional skill folder paths, remote skill URLs to fetch from, and semantic auto-match settings (injection count and cosine-similarity threshold) for automatic skill context injection.

nodes.name: variable.ts
nodes.summary: Config text interpolation: expands `{env:VAR}` environment substitutions and inline `{file:path}` references (skipping `//`-commented lines, supporting `~/` paths) by reading file contents as JSON-escaped strings, with configurable missing-file behavior.

nodes.name: substitute
nodes.summary: Applies `{env:VAR}` and `{file:path}` substitutions to raw config text: env vars expand inline, file tokens resolve relative to the config file's directory (`~/` aware) and are injected JSON-string-escaped, and missing files either throw InvalidError or expand to empty per the `missing` option.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Workspace adapter registry: resolves workspace types to adapters by combining module-level builtins (worktree) with a project-scoped registration map, so plugins can register custom workspace types per project or globally via ProjectID.global.

nodes.name: getAdapter
nodes.summary: Returns the project-scoped custom adapter for a workspace type, falling back to the builtin registry, and throws for unknown adapter types.

nodes.name: listAdapters
nodes.summary: Projects all registered adapters for a project into WorkspaceAdapterEntry summaries (type, name, description) for listing available workspace types.

nodes.name: registeredAdapters
nodes.summary: Merges builtin adapters with any project-scoped custom registrations, with custom entries overriding builtins of the same type key.

nodes.name: registerAdapter
nodes.summary: Registers a custom workspace adapter scoped to a project ID; pass ProjectID.global to install it for all projects.

nodes.name: worktree.ts
nodes.summary: Built-in workspace adapter implementing git worktree workspaces: configure derives name/branch/directory, create/remove delegate to the Worktree service, list enumerates existing worktrees, and target reports the local directory — all lazily importing the Effect runtime and services to avoid load cycles.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dynamic import() inside a shared loadWorktree() helper so the adapter module stays decoupled from the heavy Effect runtime graph at import time.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Developer guide for the debug workspace plugin: how to register it in `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`, run the standalone workspace server script, and how the file-based handshake (port/id written to /tmp and watched by the server) simulates a remote workspace locally, one debug workspace at a time.

nodes.name: debug-workspace-plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Dev-only OpenCode plugin registering a `debug` workspace type that simulates a remote environment: on create it picks a random port, writes the handshake file consumed by the workspace server script, and polls the health endpoint until the fake remote server is up.

nodes.name: waitForHealth
nodes.summary: Polls `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/global/health` every 250ms for up to 30 seconds until the debug workspace server responds OK, throwing on timeout.

nodes.name: writeDebugData
nodes.summary: Atomically writes the debug server handshake file (port, workspace id, env) via temp-file-plus-rename so the watching server script picks up complete data and restarts with the new workspace info.

nodes.name: DebugWorkspacePlugin
nodes.summary: Plugin entry point registering the `debug` workspace adapter: create spins up an external server via the handshake file and waits for health, remove is a no-op, and target routes to `http://localhost:<port>/` as a remote workspace.

nodes.name: schema.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the branded WorkspaceID schema (strings prefixed `wrk`) with an `ascending` static factory that generates sortable, ULID-style workspace identifiers.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Core control-plane type surface: the WorkspaceInfo/WorkspaceListedInfo schemas, the WorkspaceAdapterEntry descriptor, the local-vs-remote Target union, and the WorkspaceAdapter interface (configure/create/list/remove/target) that every workspace type implements.

nodes.name: util.ts
nodes.summary: Provides `waitEvent`, an Effect wrapper around the GlobalBus that suspends until a matching global event arrives, an abort signal fires, or a timeout elapses — the synchronization primitive behind workspace creation and sync fencing.

nodes.name: waitEvent
nodes.summary: Blocks as an Effect until a GlobalBus event matches the predicate, failing on abort signal, timeout, or handler error, with complete listener/timer cleanup wired through Effect.callback's cancellation return.

nodes.name: workspace-context.ts
nodes.summary: AsyncLocalStorage-backed ambient context carrying the current WorkspaceID across async boundaries, with provide/restore wrappers and a safe `workspaceID` getter that returns undefined when called outside any context.

nodes.name: workspace.sql.ts
nodes.summary: Drizzle schema for the `workspace` SQLite table: branded WorkspaceID primary key, type/name/branch/directory columns, JSON-encoded extra data, a cascading project foreign key, and a time_used column defaulting to now.
nodes.languageNotes: Follows the repo's snake_case Drizzle field convention so column names never need string overrides.

nodes.name: workspace
nodes.summary: SQLite table persisting registered workspaces: id, type, name, branch, directory, JSON extra payload, owning project (cascade delete), and last-used timestamp.

nodes.name: workspace.ts
nodes.summary: The Workspace control-plane service (~1000 lines): persists workspaces to SQLite, drives the adapter lifecycle (create/remove/list/syncList), maintains remote-workspace SSE sync loops in a FiberMap with exponential-backoff reconnects, replays sync/history events, and implements session warping — moving a session between workspaces by replaying its event log in batches and stealing remote ownership.
nodes.languageNotes: Service methods are Effect.fn generators closed over a shared FiberMap; Schema.TaggedErrorClass errors double as typed wire errors, and the legacy Promise-based adapter calls are bridged back into Effect via EffectBridge.fromPromise.

nodes.name: fromRow
nodes.summary: Maps a WorkspaceTable row into the camelCase Workspace Info shape, including the time_used to timeUsed translation.

nodes.name: synced
nodes.summary: Checks the EventSequenceTable to verify every aggregate in the given per-session sequence state has caught up to its expected seq — the sync fence predicate used by waitForSync.

nodes.name: SyncHttpError
nodes.summary: Tagged error for failed workspace sync HTTP calls, carrying the response status and optional body.

nodes.name: WorkspaceNotFoundError
nodes.summary: Tagged error raised when an operation references a workspace ID that does not exist.

nodes.name: SessionEventsNotFoundError
nodes.summary: Tagged error raised when attempting to warp a session that has no persisted events to replay.

nodes.name: SessionWarpHttpError
nodes.summary: Tagged error for failed session-warp HTTP batch or steal requests, carrying workspace ID, session ID, status, and body.

nodes.name: SyncTimeoutError
nodes.summary: Tagged error thrown when waiting for the sync fence times out, carrying the expected per-aggregate sequence state.

nodes.name: SyncAbortedError
nodes.summary: Tagged error thrown when sync fencing is aborted via signal, wrapping the abort cause as a defect.

nodes.name: Service
nodes.summary: Context.Service tag for the Workspace control-plane interface: create, sessionWarp, list, syncList, get, remove, status, isSyncing, waitForSync, and startWorkspaceSyncing.

nodes.name: data-migration.sql.ts
nodes.summary: Drizzle schema for the `data_migration` SQLite table that tracks completed data migrations by name and completion timestamp.

nodes.name: data_migration
nodes.summary: SQLite bookkeeping table (name primary key, time_completed) recording which one-off data migrations have already run.

nodes.name: data-migration.ts
nodes.summary: Data-migration runner service: executes registered named migrations inside a forked background fiber, skipping any already recorded in the data_migration table and logging-and-ignoring failures so boot is never blocked; currently ships an empty migration list.
nodes.languageNotes: Migrations run via Effect.forkScoped so they stay resumable until their completion row is written.

nodes.name: Service
nodes.summary: Context.Service tag for the DataMigration service, exposing the background migration-runner interface to the rest of the app layer.

nodes.name: app-runtime.ts
nodes.summary: The application's composition root: AppLayer merges ~50 service default layers (config, storage, sessions, providers, MCP, LSP, skills, workspace, worktree, data migration, etc.) over the Instance and Observability layers, and AppRuntime exposes the ManagedRuntime's runSync/runPromise/runFork entry points with run-service attachment pre-applied.
nodes.languageNotes: ManagedRuntime is built with a shared memoMap so layer construction is memoized process-wide; every run* method pipes effects through the attach() wrapper from run-service.

nodes.name: bootstrap-runtime.ts
nodes.summary: Minimal pre-boot runtime that merges only the services needed before the full app layer exists (Config, Plugin, ShareNext, Format, LSP, File, FileWatcher, Vcs, Snapshot, Bus) over the Observability layer.

nodes.name: bridge.ts
nodes.summary: Effect-to-Promise bridge that preserves ambient context: fromPromise runs a JS async callback while reinstalling the legacy Instance/WorkspaceContext AsyncLocalStorage, and make produces a promise/fork/run bridge that re-enters Effect with the captured instance and workspace refs attached.
nodes.languageNotes: Node's AsyncLocalStorage propagates across await boundaries where Effect's InstanceRef/WorkspaceRef do not — the bridge restores ALS before invoking callbacks that may spawn nested Effect runtimes.

nodes.name: fromPromise
nodes.summary: Runs a Promise-returning callback as an Effect while restoring legacy Instance and Workspace AsyncLocalStorage contexts, so nested AppRuntime.runPromise calls inside the callback keep their ambient instance/workspace state.

nodes.name: make
nodes.summary: Builds a Shape bridge (promise/fork/run) that captures the current InstanceRef/WorkspaceRef with an AsyncLocalStorage fallback and re-executes wrapped effects with the original Effect context provided, translating exits back into succeed/failCause.

nodes.name: config-service.ts
nodes.summary: Factory for config-backed Context services: given a service id and a map of Effect Config definitions it generates a typed service class with a `layer` for injecting pre-parsed values (tests) and a `defaultLayer` that parses config once from the active ConfigProvider.

nodes.name: Service
nodes.summary: Class factory deriving a Context.Service from a record of Effect Config fields, generating static `layer` (inject parsed values) and `defaultLayer` (parse via Config.all) layers so env names, defaults, and validation stay in one place.
